title: How a prefix changes a verb of motion

blocks.text: Lesson text quoted from the Defense Language Institute Russian Basic Course, Grammar Reference Books I (1970) and II (1965), a US Government work in the public domain (https://www.fsi-language-courses.org/russian/courses/dli-russian-basic-course), from the English Wikipedia's article «Russian grammar», section «Verbs of motion» (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_grammar#Verbs_of_motion, CC BY-SA 4.0), and from the English Wiktionary's entries for each verb, named where a table is given (https://en.wiktionary.org/, CC BY-SA 4.0). Exercises: sentences and translations from Tatoeba (https://tatoeba.org/, CC BY 2.0 FR) and sentences from the library's public-domain books; the answer is always the word the sentence has.

Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.

In addition to the meanings conveyed by the prefix and the simplex motion verb, prepositional phrases also contribute to the expression of path in Russian. Thus, it is important to consider the whole verb phrase when examining verbs of motion.

In some verbs of motion, adding a prefix requires a different stem shape: A. **идти** → **-йти** 'go (on foot)': For prefixes ending in a consonant, an -o- is added in all forms, e.g.: **войти**. **й** is lost in the conjugated forms of **прийти**, e.g.: **приду** 'I will come'. B. **ездить** → **-езжать** 'go (by conveyance)': For prefixes ending in a consonant, a hard sign (**ъ**) is added before –**ехать** and –**езжать**, e.g.: **въезжать** 'enter (by conveyance)'.

C. **бе́гать** → **-бега́ть** 'run': The formation of the verb remains the same, but stress shifts from the stem to the endings, e.g.: **убега́ть** 'run away'. D. **пла́вать** → **-плыва́ть** 'swim': The vowel in the root changes to **-ы-** and the stress shifts to the endings.
E. As with non-motion verbs, in perfective verbs with the prefix **вы-**, the prefix is stressed in all forms, e.g. **вы́йдешь** 'you will go out'.

Any prefix (except "**по**-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair. Thus: Original pair, imperfective: repeated — **ходить**, **ездить**, **летать**; actual — **идти**, **ехать**, **лететь**.

items: Он всегда приезжает сюда на грузовике.
Он всегда приезжал сюда на грузовике.
Он всегда будет приезжать сюда на грузовике.
Сегодня он приехал сюда на автобусе.
Сегодня он приедет сюда на автобусе.

blocks.text: Notice that with the verb "**идти**" **-о-** is inserted between the verb and the prefix if the prefix ends in a consonant.

All prefixed verbs derived from **ходить** belong to the 2nd (**И**) type of conjugation and have the same change in the stress pattern: **ходить** — **я хожу**, **ты ходишь**, etc.; **отходить** — **я отхожу**, **ты отходишь**; **подходить** — **я подхожу**, **ты подходишь**; **приходить** — **я прихожу**, **ты приходишь**; **уходить** — **я ухожу**, **ты уходишь**. All prefixed verbs derived from **езжать** (which is not used without prefix) belong to the 1st (**Е**) type of conjugation and have a fixed stress.

Any prefix (except "**по**-") added to the imperfective pair of these verbs (**носить**, **возить**, **водить** — to both "repeated" and "actual" functions) makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair which carries the meaning governed by the prefix. The verbs "**носить**", "**возить**" and "**водить**" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning.
However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.
